alignments.note: Connective δέ realized by the verse-opening Now.
Article governing a substantival adjective supplies the nominal things (rules 22, 102); the ASV writes no determiner, so the article's whole realization is that noun.
Substantival εἰδωλόθυτον rendered sacrificed to idols; head on the participial word carrying the lexeme, the generic things having gone to the article.
Inflected verb takes its supplied subject; head on the lexical verb (rule 9).
ὅτι introducing reported speech is realized by that (rule 43).
Subject we and lexical verb have belong to ἔχομεν, discontinuously across the quantifier (rule 15).
The ASV writes Knowledge with no determiner, so the article realizes nothing (rule 23).
φυσιόω is glossed puff up; the up is part of the English gloss of the verb and the head is the verb word.
The ASV writes love with no determiner, so the article realizes nothing (rule 23).
οἰκοδομεῖ → edifieth; the packet's gloss note records the Greek buildeth up but the ASV writes one word.

review_notes: Both εἰδωλοθύτων phrases in this chapter are analysed with the article taking the supplied nominal things and the adjective taking sacrificed to idols (rules 22, 102); reading things as the adjective's own generic completion under rule 17 with the article unrepresented remains defensible, but rule 102 keeps a supplied nominal inside the phrase an article governs.
Both anarthrous-in-English nouns after ἡ (γνῶσις, ἀγάπη) leave their articles unrepresented under rule 23.
